title: Holy Saturday
hookLine: the day of silence; the Church says he went down to free the dead (CCC 632–635)
carry: god is in the silence too

cards: Everyone knows a day in between. The day after the phone call and before the funeral. The day you wait for a test result.
Nothing happens, and it's the heaviest day of the week. The Gospels say almost nothing about the Saturday after the cross. Matthew mentions guards posted at the tomb.
Luke gives it one line: the women rested on the Sabbath, according to the commandment. No words from Jesus. No miracles.

A sealed tomb, and people sitting at home with spices they can't use yet. The Church keeps that day on purpose: on Holy Saturday there's no Mass during the day, and the tabernacle is still empty. Catholics wait.

teach.b: But the Church doesn't say nothing happened. It says something happened where no one could see. In the old Apostles' Creed, Catholics say: "He descended into hell."
That word trips people up. Here it doesn't mean the place of the damned.

teach.h: NOT THE DAMNED: THE REALM OF THE DEAD.
teach.b: The Catechism explains it means the realm of all the dead, what the Hebrew Bible calls Sheol. Jesus really died, the Church says, so he went where the dead go.
Not to be stuck there: to open it, to bring out the just who had died before him, all the way back to Adam and Eve. The First Letter of Peter says he went and preached to the spirits in prison.
Eastern Christians paint it. Their Easter icon doesn't show an empty tomb.

teach.h: BROKEN DOORS, ADAM BY THE WRIST.
teach.b: It shows Christ standing on broken doors, the locks scattered, pulling Adam and Eve up out of their graves by the wrists.

teach.h: A GREAT SILENCE ON THE EARTH.
teach.b: And an ancient sermon read on Holy Saturday in the Church's daily prayer, the Office of Readings, begins by saying there is a great silence on the earth, because the King is asleep.
Then it follows him down, looking for Adam. So on the quietest day of the year, the Church says God was at work in the deepest place. Nobody saw it.
Silence isn't the same as absence.

how: On Holy Saturday Catholic churches celebrate no Mass during the day; the tabernacle stays empty, and the Church waits in prayer until the Easter Vigil after nightfall.

o: the day of the Last Supper and the foot washing
the day Jesus rode into Jerusalem on a donkey
the quiet day between the cross and Easter

games.q: what's inside the silent day — tap the pairs.
p: Christ pulling Adam and Eve out
a great silence on the earth

s: 'he descended into hell' means he went to the place of the damned
the Catechism says it means the realm of all the dead, to free the just who died before him.
the Gospels describe Holy Saturday in detail
they say almost nothing: Matthew mentions a guard at the tomb, and Luke says the women rested on the Sabbath.
there is no Mass during the day on Holy Saturday
the Church waits until the Easter Vigil after dark.

games.q: you're one of the women from Galilee. the spices are ready, and the Sabbath has begun. what do you do?
games.why: Luke says they rested on the Sabbath, according to the commandment. his one line about the day is a line about waiting.

practice: Put the phone face down, out of reach, and hold one thing that's still in between: a result, a reply, a healing, a decision someone else has to make.
Hold it the way the women held their spices, ready and not yet used; you don't have to understand it or fix it.
If you pray, you can simply stay in God's presence without words; if you don't, you can notice what silence actually sounds like.

wordCard.voice: Holy Saturday. The silent day between the cross and the morning, when the Church says he went down to free the dead. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: Sheol, the realm of the dead in the Hebrew Bible. what the Creed's hell means here.

carryVoice: Your line: god is in the silence too. The tomb is sealed, and morning is coming. That's day sixty-seven.
